title: Geometric specialization slices of oriented nearby cycles
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite-type morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\Lambda$ a commutative ring killed by an integer $m\geq1$, and $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Use $V_f$, $R\Psi_f$ and its counit-defined ordinary comparisons from [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. A geometric specialization $b\to a$ means a morphism $c:S_{(b)}\to S_{(a)}$ over $S$ between strict localizations [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Put $X_{(a)}=X\times_SS_{(a)}$, $X_{(b)}=X\times_SS_{(b)}$, $X_a=X\times_Sa$, and let $j_b:X_{(b)}\to X_{(a)}$ and $i_a:X_a\to X_{(a)}$ be the maps induced by $c$ and the geometric closed point $a\to S_{(a)}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The specialization gives a geometric morphism $e^f_{a,b}:(X_a)_{\mathrm{Et}}\to V_f$ whose composition with a geometric point $x$ of $X_a$ is the oriented point $(x,b,c)$. Its inverse image is exact, and there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$e^{f,*}_{a,b}R\Psi_fK\simeq i_a^*Rj_{b,*}(K|_{X_{(b)}}).$$
For every $T\to S$ and geometric specialization $b_T\to a_T$ mapping to $b\to a$, this isomorphism identifies the pullback along $e^{f_T}_{a_T,b_T}$ of the ordinary oriented comparison with the ordinary comparison between the displayed sliced complexes, defined by the direct-image counits and inverse-image composition comparisons. This compatibility also holds for successive base changes. The functors $e^{f,*}_{a,b}$, as $a,b,c$ vary, detect cohomology vanishing: for $A\in D(V_f,\Lambda)$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$, $\mathcal H^i(A)=0$ for all $i\leq r$ if and only if $\mathcal H^i(e^{f,*}_{a,b}A)=0$ for all $i\leq r$ and all slices.

source.place: Expose XI, 1.4 and 1.9 (universal property and functoriality), 2.2--2.3 (specialization sections), 2.7 (strict-local limits), 4.3 (nearby cycles); specialization-slice consequence. Also Orgogozo, Modifications et cycles proches, section 1, pp. 2--3 (local archival PDF WANTED).

proof.text:
Write $d_a:X_a\to X$ and $\pi_a:(X_a)_{\mathrm{Et}}\to\mathbf{Set}$. The two morphisms $d_a$ and $b\pi_a$ to $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $S_{\mathrm{Et}}$, with the $2$-arrow $b\pi_a\Rightarrow a\pi_a=fd_a$ specified by $c$, define $e=e^f_{a,b}$ by [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Its composite with a geometric point $x$ is $(x,b,c)$. The inverse image on constant modules is exact by [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], for this arbitrary geometric morphism; no factorization into scheme maps is needed. For a triple $C=(U\to V\leftarrow W)$, write $V_a=a^*V$, $W_b=b^*W$ and $c^*:V_a\to V_b$. The universal-product formula gives
$$e^{-1}h_C^\#=\coprod_{v\in V_a,\ w\in W_b,\ c^*v=\operatorname{image}(w)}h_{U_{a,v}},$$
where $U_{a,v}$ is the fibre over $v$ of $U\times_Sa\to V\times_Sa$. These are sheaves represented by the indicated etale objects of $X_a$.

source.place: Exposé XI, 1.4 (explicit inverse image), 1.9 and 2.2 (specialization arrow).

proof.text:
We construct a morphism before testing stalks. Put $r_b:X_{(b)}\to X$. Fix $C,v,w$ as in step 1. The pointed-neighbourhood limit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] gives lifts $\widetilde v:S_{(a)}\to V$ and $\widetilde w:S_{(b)}\to W$. The germ bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-strictly-henselian-open-sections-stalk], applied to the representable sheaf on $S_{(b)}$, identifies lifts with their closed geometric germs; strict henselianity is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]. Thus the relation $c^*v=\operatorname{image}(w)$ says that the composite of $\widetilde w$ with $W\to V$ is $\widetilde v c$; it is equality of the same pointed-neighbourhood projections. Put $E_v=U\times_V S_{(a)}$. It is an etale object of $X_{(a)}$: in its small etale site it is the pullback of $U\times_SS_{(a)}\to X\times_SV\times_SS_{(a)}$ along the section defined by $\widetilde v$, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] applies. Its fibre over $a$ is $U_{a,v}$. There is a specific map
$$\ell_{C,v,w}:E_v\times_{S_{(a)}}S_{(b)}\longrightarrow U\times_VW,$$
with projections to $U$ and to $W$ given respectively by $E_v\to U$ and $\widetilde w$. The equality just checked is exactly the fibre-product condition.

source.place: Exposé XI, 1.4 and 4.3; pointed lifts from strict localizations, 2.7.

proof.text:
For a module sheaf $F$ on $X$, set $B_F=i_a^*j_{b,*}r_b^*F$. By [lem-trf-oriented-point-cohomology], $\psi_f^{-1}h_C^\#=h_{U\times_VW}$, hence $(\psi_{f,*}F)(C)=F(U\times_VW)$. For each $v,w$ define the homomorphism
$$F(U\times_VW)\longrightarrow (r_b^*F)(E_v\times_{S_{(a)}}S_{(b)})=(j_{b,*}r_b^*F)(E_v)\longrightarrow B_F(U_{a,v}).$$
The first arrow is inverse-image restriction along $\ell_{C,v,w}$, and the last is the inverse-image unit for $i_a$ evaluated on $E_v$. The direct-image and module-unit formulas are those of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Combine these arrows on the disjoint components of $e^{-1}h_C^\#$ from step 1. If $C'\to C$ is a triple map, its maps on $E_v$ and on $U\times_VW$ commute with $\ell$, by equality of their two projections. Restrictions and inverse-image units are natural, so these homomorphisms commute with every triple restriction. They are therefore a morphism of sheaves $\psi_{f,*}F\to e_*B_F$ on the triple site. Adjunction gives an actual natural sheaf morphism
$$\chi_F:e^*\psi_{f,*}F\longrightarrow i_a^*j_{b,*}r_b^*F.$$
This construction uses sections on all objects, rather than an inference that stalk isomorphisms glue.

source.place: Exposé XI, 1.4 and 4.3 (triple-site inverse image and section restrictions).

proof.text:
Choose a bounded-below injective complex $I$ representing $K$, using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Apply $\chi$ degreewise and then the right-derived unit for $j_{b,*}$ to define
$$\alpha_K:e^*R\Psi_fK=e^*\psi_{f,*}I\xrightarrow{\chi_I}i_a^*j_{b,*}r_b^*I\longrightarrow i_a^*Rj_{b,*}r_b^*I=i_a^*Rj_{b,*}r_b^*K.$$
This is a global derived morphism. The last arrow is the unit in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], so it does not assume that $r_b^*I$ is injective or $j_{b,*}$-acyclic. A map of coefficients is represented by a chain map into injective representatives, unique up to homotopy by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Naturality of $\chi$ and of the derived unit makes the displayed map commute with these chain maps. Additive functors preserve homotopies; a change between injective representatives is a homotopy equivalence by that same node. Thus the construction is independent of representatives and natural in $K$.

source.place: Exposé XI, 4.3; derivation of the explicit restriction morphism. Stacks Tags 070G (K-injective computation) and 09T5 (derived adjunction).

proof.text: Now test this existing map. At a geometric point $x$ of $X_a$, the left stalk is $R\Gamma(M_x,r_x^*K)$ by [lem-trf-oriented-point-cohomology], with $M_x=X_{(x)}\times_{S_{(a)}}S_{(b)}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], $S_{(b)}\to S_{(a)}$ and its base change $j_b$ are affine, so $j_b$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The strict-local stalk formula [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] computes the right stalk by the same tube: [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance] identifies the strict localization of $X_{(a)}$ at $x$ with that of $X$, because $X_{(a)}\to X$ is a base change of a strict localization. This includes extension of the chosen geometric fields. The functorial maps of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality] identify the structural maps of the tubes. The scalar comparisons [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison] and [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] allow applying the abelian stalk formula to constant-module coefficients, and preserve the restriction maps. All cohomology sheaves are torsion since $mK=0$; no invertibility of $m$ is needed.

source.place: Exposé XI, 2.7 and 4.3; Stacks Tag 03Q9 (canonical derived stalk map), Tags 05WR and 0GIP (strict-local invariance).

proof.text: The stalk map of $\alpha_K$ is the restriction map to that common tube, not merely an unspecified isomorphism of its endpoints. Indeed $\chi_I$ sends a representative section on $U\times_VW$ to its restriction along $\ell_{C,v,w}$; at $x$ the maps $\ell$ converge to $M_x\to U\times_VW$. The derived unit in step 4 is the canonical comparison from sections to derived sections. These are precisely the two canonical restriction maps in [lem-trf-oriented-point-cohomology] and [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula]. Both identify the stalk map with the identity of $R\Gamma(M_x,r_x^*K)$. Consequently every stalk of $\alpha_K$ is invertible. Forget the scalar action and apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative]; the exact conservative scalar-forgetting functor of [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison] then makes $\alpha_K$ invertible in modules. This is the only use of derived stalk conservativity: it proves invertibility of the map already constructed.

source.place: Exposé XI, 2.7 and 4.3; Stacks Tag 03Q9, normalization by canonical restriction.

proof.text:
Fix $h:T\to S$, write $\widetilde h:X_T\to X$, $v:V_{f_T}\to V_f$, $e_T=e^{f_T}_{a_T,b_T}$, and denote the induced maps by $q_a:X_{a_T}\to X_a$, $q_A:X_{T,(a_T)}\to X_{(a)}$, $q_B:X_{T,(b_T)}\to X_{(b)}$. Write $i_T,j_T,r_{b_T}$ for the three maps over $T$. Thus $q_Ai_T=i_aq_a$, $q_Aj_T=j_bq_B$, and $r_bq_B=\widetilde h r_{b_T}$. The universal product gives $ve_T\cong eq_a$ with coherent projection identifications. Let $K_b=r_b^*K$. Define $E:q_A^*Rj_{b,*}K_b\to Rj_{T,*}q_B^*K_b$ to be the adjunct of
$$j_T^*q_A^*Rj_{b,*}K_b\cong q_B^*j_b^*Rj_{b,*}K_b\xrightarrow{q_B^*\varepsilon_{j_b}}q_B^*K_b.$$
Define the sliced map $\gamma=i_T^*E$ after $q_a^*i_a^*\cong i_T^*q_A^*$, with target coefficients $q_B^*K_b\cong r_{b_T}^*\widetilde h^*K$. Its type is
$$\gamma:q_a^*i_a^*Rj_{b,*}K_b\longrightarrow i_T^*Rj_{T,*}r_{b_T}^*\widetilde h^*K.$$
These are the ordinary adjunctions of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]; [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] fixes the scheme inverse-image comparisons. No Cartesian assertion about the square of $j_b,j_T$ is required.

source.place: Exposé XI, 1.9 and 4.3; definition of the ordinary counit-mate comparison.

proof.text:
We check the sheaf comparison square on generators, so that the later derived equality is global. Base change $C$ to $C_T$ and choose a component $(v_T,w_T)$ of $e_T^{-1}v^{-1}h_C^\#$; it maps to $(v,w)$ in step 1. Let $D=U\times_VW$, $D_T=D\times_X X_T$, $E_v$ be as in step 2, and $E_{v_T}$ its analogue. There is a commutative square
$$\begin{matrix}E_{v_T}\times_{T_{(a_T)}}T_{(b_T)}&\xrightarrow{\ell_T}&D_T\\ \downarrow k&&\downarrow\\ E_v\times_{S_{(a)}}S_{(b)}&\xrightarrow{\ell}&D.\end{matrix}$$
The $U$-projections agree by fibre-product functoriality and the $W$-projections agree by the compatibility of the pointed-neighbourhood lifts with $c,c_T$. Hence $\ell k$ equals the other composite. For $s\in F(D)$ both routes through the sheaf square send $s$ to its inverse-image restriction along this single composite, then to the closed fibre by the $i_T$-unit. Naturality of that unit gives equality of the routes on every $C$ and every component. The underived ordinary exchange sends $s$ to precisely its pullback on $D_T$: its adjunct is inverse-image composition followed by the counit, as is checked by evaluating the adjunction on $h_C^\#$. Thus this is equality for the specified ordinary sheaf mates and the specified $\chi$ maps, rather than equality of their geometric stalks.

source.place: Exposé XI, 1.4, 1.9 and 4.3; explicit restriction-square verification on triples.

proof.text:
Derive the square of step 8 with its units. For an injective representative $I$ of $K$, take an injective replacement $\widetilde h^*I\to J$ over $X_T$. The ordinary oriented map is represented by $v^*\psi_{f,*}I\to\psi_{f_T,*}\widetilde h^*I\to\psi_{f_T,*}J$. On the sliced side apply the $j_b,j_T$ derived units to the sheaf square, and use naturality of $\chi$ for the map $\widetilde h^*I\to J$. After replacing the complexes on $X_{(b)}$ and $X_{T,(b_T)}$ by K-injectives, the two composites are images of that same sheaf square. Maps into these replacements and changes of replacements are determined up to homotopy by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; the universal derived units in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] therefore give equality of the resulting derived transformations. The adjunctions have the original composite counits, by [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization]. Thus the represented oriented and sliced arrows are exactly the mates defining $\beta$ and $\gamma$, not different arrows with the same endpoints. With $\rho:e_T^*v^*\cong q_a^*e^*$ the result is the typed equality
$$\alpha_{\widetilde h^*K,T}\circ e_T^*\beta_{\widetilde h,h,K}=\gamma\circ q_a^*\alpha_K\circ\rho_{R\Psi_fK}.$$
This proves the required counit-mate identification.

source.place: Exposé XI, 1.9 and 4.3; Stacks Tags 070G, 09T5 and 0D6E, with the explicit sheaf square from step 8.

proof.text:
For $U\xrightarrow{k}T\xrightarrow{h}S$, write $p_A,p_B,p_a$ for the maps from the strict-local and fibre schemes over $U$ to those over $T$. Before mating, the two $j$-squares have inverse-image identifications
$$j_U^*p_A^*q_A^*\cong p_B^*j_T^*q_A^*\cong p_B^*q_B^*j_b^*.$$
Their composite is the inverse-image identification for $(q_Ap_A,q_Bp_B)$: the fibre-product projections agree and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] uses precisely these comparisons. Part 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] therefore gives $E_{hk}=(E_kq_B^*)\circ p_A^*E_h$. Restricting by $i_U^*$ and using $p_Ai_U=i_Tp_a$ gives $\gamma_{hk}=\gamma_k\circ p_a^*\gamma_h$ with its coefficient identifications. The identical pasting statement applied to $v\psi_{f_T}\cong\psi_f\widetilde h$ gives $\beta_{hk}=\beta_k\circ v_k^*\beta_h$. Parts 2--3 of the mate-pasting node and [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] ensure these are the canonical derived composite adjunctions. The identifications $\rho$ compose by uniqueness in the universal product. Inserting these three equalities into step 9 proves the compatibility for successive base changes, as an equality of natural transformations. No faithfulness of derived stalks is asserted.

source.place: Exposé XI, 1.9 (successive squares); mate-pasting identities, Stacks Tags 0E46 and 0E47.

proof.text: For the final clause, let $A\in D(V_f,\Lambda)$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$. Exactness in step 1 gives $\mathcal H^i(e^*A)=e^*\mathcal H^i(A)$, so vanishing of the former follows from vanishing of the latter. Conversely every point $z_{x,b,c}$ in [lem-trf-oriented-product-points-conservative] factors as $e_{a,b}x'$, taking $a=f(x)$ and the geometric point $x'$ of $X_a$ supplied by $x$ and its common geometric field. If all slice cohomology sheaves vanish for $i\le r$, each such point kills $\mathcal H^i(A)$. Apply the sheaf-level conservative family of that node to $0\to\mathcal H^i(A)$; the cohomology sheaf is zero. This works for unbounded $A$, since the inverse images are exact and applied termwise, and for every integer $r$.

source.place: Exposé XI, 2.3--2.4 (points and conservativity), with exact constant-coefficient inverse images.
